findings: All tested corrections improve national JJAS rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -1.311; corrected -0.078 to -0.025). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.

Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug), Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Aug), Power Transformation (Aug) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Aug), and the tercile (RPS) passes are none. Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Gamma Quantile Mapping Jun, Gamma Quantile Mapping Sep, Power Transformation Jul, Power Transformation Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling JJAS, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jul, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Jun, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Sep and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Sep.

Variance Scaling (unbounded) is at least as good as Mean-Variance Scaling in the national aggregate for every tested target and period, on amounts and unblended terciles (JJAS CRPSS -0.027 vs -0.028 in 1993–2016, -0.016 vs -0.018 in 2017–2025). Its JJAS amount screening pass does not survive the family-wide correction. Members clipped to 0 mm in the months: 1.3%–9.9% with Mean-Variance Scaling, 0.2%–1.4% with this method. This need not hold in each region; see the tables for the JJAS R1+R2 rainfall domain.

Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: —); it passes the screening for none, but its JJAS amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (-0.040 vs -0.028). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.

The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on JJAS terciles (-0.080 to -0.044 vs -0.017) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause.
Jun and Sep remain hard: every method has negative amount skill over 2017–2025.

No tested method demonstrates a statistically significant improvement over Mean-Variance Scaling for the published tercile probabilities under this validation protocol, although several have slightly higher point estimates. Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores JJAS blended RPSS +0.025 against +0.027, confirmed for none. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS -0.036 against -0.028, confirmed for Jun, Aug and Sep; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: Variance Scaling (unbounded) (Jul, Aug), Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Aug), Power Transformation (Aug) and Gamma Quantile Mapping (Aug).

The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, JJAS RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.010 after the blend against 0.066 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Jun the fitted weight on climatology is 0.75 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.80 with Mean-Variance Scaling.

Choosing by training scores can backfire. For Jul, SEL-A chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean CRPS (Δ +0.194 mm, 95% interval -0.094 to +0.517 mm; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 3 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2020 and 2024); for Sep, SEL-P chose Scaled Distribution Mapping from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.001 to +0.003; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2018 and 2024); for JJAS, SEL-P chose Delta Change from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.004, 95% interval -0.000 to +0.009; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 2 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2018 and 2023). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.

Where the confirmed amount gains come from (climate groups from each fold’s training years; contributions add up to the national difference from Mean-Variance Scaling): Variance Scaling (unbounded) in Jul (Δ CRPS -0.139 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.014 mm (10%; 4% of the area), mixed -0.042 mm (30%; 9% of the area), always wet -0.083 mm (60%; 88% of the area); Variance Scaling (unbounded) in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.129 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.008 mm (6%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.018 mm (14%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.103 mm (80%; 95% of the area); Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.096 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.004 mm (5%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.012 mm (13%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.079 mm (83%; 95% of the area); Power Transformation in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.124 mm): all ≤ 1 mm -0.008 mm (6%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.017 mm (14%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.099 mm (80%; 95% of the area); Gamma Quantile Mapping in Aug (Δ CRPS -0.128 mm): all ≤ 1 mm +0.000 mm (-0%; 2% of the area), mixed -0.012 mm (9%; 3% of the area), always wet -0.116 mm (91%; 95% of the area).

No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.
observations: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly totals, averaged from 0.05° to 0.25°

config_contents.name: may_jjas
config_contents.description: Rainfall-amount bias-correction benchmark: May-initialized ECMWF SEAS5, JJAS season and its calendar months, every 0.25 deg cell of Ethiopia (docs/47).

benchmark.gate_rule: Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2025 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

raw.label: Raw ECMWF (no correction)
raw.definition: x' = x (the uncorrected model; baseline, not a candidate)

ls.label: Linear Scaling
ls.definition: x' = x * mu_obs / mu_model (multiplicative mean correction; ratio 1 where mu_model < 0.1 mm)

mvs.label: Mean-Variance Scaling (operational)
mvs.definition: x' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mm

vs.label: Variance Scaling (unbounded)
vs.definition: Same algebra and the same r = 1 fallback (sd_model < 1 mm) as MVS, without the 0.5-2 ratio limits

sqrt_mvs.label: Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling
sqrt_mvs.definition: MVS applied to sqrt(x) (r limits 0.5-2; r = 1 if the sqrt-space sd < 0.1), clipped at 0 and squared back (docs/36)

pt.label: Power Transformation
pt.definition: x' = a x^b: b (0.1-3) matches the coefficient of variation where reachable (bound hits reported), a the mean

dc.label: Delta Change
dc.definition: Training-year CHIRPS totals times a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (a in 0.2-5): historical scenarios, not corrected members

loci.label: Local Intensity Scaling
loci.definition: Model threshold with the observed frequency of totals above 1 mm, then intensity scaling above it (designed for daily rainfall; here monthly or seasonal totals)

eqm.label: Empirical Quantile Mapping
eqm.definition: x' = Q_obs(F_model(x)) with the dry policy; constant-ratio extrapolation outside the training range

gqm.label: Gamma Quantile Mapping
gqm.definition: x' = G_obs^-1(G_model(x)), G = dry mass (<= 1 mm) + gamma by weighted maximum likelihood, with the dry policy; linear scaling where fewer than 3 wet values

dqm.label: Detrended Quantile Mapping
dqm.definition: a * EQM(x / a), a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (0.2-5): removes and reapplies the bounded ratio; exact preservation of the final mean anomaly is not guaranteed

qdm.label: Quantile Delta Mapping
qdm.definition: x' = Q_obs(tau) * x / Q_model(tau), tau = rank of x in the forecast ensemble; change capped at 5 and replaced by Q_obs(tau) where Q_model(tau) <= 1 mm (both reported), so preservation is partial there

sdm.label: Scaled Distribution Mapping
sdm.definition: Switanek et al. (2017) precipitation steps 1-7: gamma fits, recurrence intervals interpolated to the forecast's length, scaled CDF, rain-member count; model climatology with equal-year weights

cdft.label: CDF-transform
cdft.definition: F_obs,f = F_obs(F_model^-1(F_forecast)); x' = F_obs,f^-1(F_forecast(x)); implementation choices: model and forecast first scaled to the CHIRPS mean, values stay within the scaled forecast range

mvs_zero_guard.label: MVS with all-zero guard (variant)
mvs_zero_guard.definition: Operational MVS, but corrected totals are 0 mm where every training year has exactly 0 mm (a documented modelling choice, not a physical rule)

config_contents.name: may_jjas_ratio_limits
config_contents.description: MVS ratio-limit study: May-initialized ECMWF SEAS5, JJAS season and its calendar months, every 0.25 deg cell of Ethiopia (docs/47). Operational MVS (spread ratio limited to 0.5-2) against the same correction with limits 1/3-3, 1/4-4 and none.

recommendation_rule.description: Rule by which the platform suggests a bias-correction method for each cycle, target and product (scripts/bias_recommend.py, docs/47). Fixed before the independent validation seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision; it never changes the published forecast.
recommendation_rule.historical: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 (false discovery rate) across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.

changes.note: Decided by the project lead after the sensitivity analyses (33-year and pooled evidence, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg) had been seen; the decisions are recomputed from the p-values each benchmark stored, within the same families. The benchmarks keep their own Holm decisions as run.

recommendation_rule.choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.

validation.rule: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'.

statuses.keep: Keep the operational method: no method is confirmed better on the historical evidence.
statuses.candidate: Confirmed better on the historical evidence; independent validation seasons are still being collected.
statuses.recommended: Confirmed better on the historical evidence and not worse over the independent validation seasons.
statuses.not_supported: Confirmed better on the historical evidence but worse over the independent validation seasons.
